lessons.text: **Locomotion works but is slow.** The athlete jogs at ~1.6 m/s and reaches all ten waypoints in 82 % of 90-second episodes. lessons.text: **A knockdown should not cost the fighter who lands it** (`--survivor-bootstrap --ko-bonus 10`). lessons.text: **Being hit should cost what hitting pays** (`--taken-w 1.0`, with the above). Run `match2`, stopped at 31 minutes: landed hits held at 1.1 a second for 20 minutes and then fell to 0.22, glove speed and joint power with them, while the reward per episode rose. With every exchange worth nothing and punching still costing energy, not punching is the best policy. **Worse.** Its checkpoint folder holds `REJECTED.txt`, and Unity's importer passes over any run that has one. Knee kv was read as 0 and the robot fell in under a second. Fixed by making the base class (0, 0) so every group writes its full pair; compiled training model is bit-identical to before.

lessons.heading: PoKingHill — RL Optimization Log › 2026-10-08 — Phase B gates passed; three Unity plugin traps

Writing ctrl only on policy ticks left 9 of 10 physics steps with zero targets. `PolicyRunner` now rewrites the held targets in `preUpdateEvent` before every step.

lessons.heading: Training lessons (G1, Kim, Trump; 2026-10-07 to 2026-10-20) › 2. Rewards
lessons.text: **A win must pay more than surviving to the bell.** r4_a (alive 0.5, upright 0.5, win 10) converged in 130 iterations to both fighters leaning on each other for 20 s: a draw paid 40, a win 10. `reward_audit.py` checks this ("stall").

lessons.heading: Training lessons (G1, Kim, Trump; 2026-10-07 to 2026-10-20) › 2. Rewards
lessons.text: **A draw that costs the same as a loss invites stalling against a stronger opponent** (cross-body xg2: Trump 65 % undecided). Draw -20 (twice a loss) fixed the stall; termination -25 (2.5 x a draw) cut falls without passivity (careful1).

lessons.heading: Training lessons (G1, Kim, Trump; 2026-10-07 to 2026-10-20) › 2. Rewards
lessons.text: **The per-step zero clip hides penalties exactly when the policy is doing badly.** It was needed (r0_a: dying early beat the penalties; r0_b: the clipped sum was always 0 and only entropy trained), but on the fight rungs it binds on 18-19 % of steps and erases 12-13 % of the penalty mass (walker and get-up: 0.1 %). Terminal terms and the potential sit outside it. Turning it off for a fine-tune did not help: `noclip1` (34 % of steps net negative once the penalties reached PPO) lost to careful1 29 / 58 and to the control 38 / 54. Keep the clip; reconsider it only for a ladder from scratch.

lessons.heading: Training lessons (G1, Kim, Trump; 2026-10-07 to 2026-10-20) › 2. Rewards
lessons.text: **Shaping that is not a potential difference can be farmed.** `ring_advantage` is flat while pushing from the inside (r4att_a learned only to stop falling); `push_out` needed a per-episode cap; in the four-way rung `opp_radius` can pay 32 per round, more than a win (30). The potential version (`r4pbrs`) did not reach careful1 in 400 iterations (loses 80 % to it): the hand-shaped terms carried behaviour the potential does not replace quickly.

lessons.heading: Training lessons (G1, Kim, Trump; 2026-10-07 to 2026-10-20) › 2. Rewards
lessons.text: **Rewards cannot place limbs.** Three runs tried to get the arms forward with rewards (shover1, shover2, hand_push) and failed; building the pose into the action path (style offsets + smoothing) worked. A styled pose switched on at once (trump_bull1) or eased in (bull2) made Trump avoid contact (11-13 % wins): a style has to fit how the body already wins.

lessons.heading: Training lessons (G1, Kim, Trump; 2026-10-07 to 2026-10-20) › 2. Rewards
lessons.text: **Dominance is normal for some tasks** (get-up: height 73 % of the shaped reward) and a warning for others (Trump's fighter: `opp_radius` 64 %).

lessons.heading: Training lessons (G1, Kim, Trump; 2026-10-07 to 2026-10-20) › 3. Opponents and curricula
lessons.text: **Frozen opponents must explore like the learner** while training (identical brains: noisy vs clean 35 / 65), unless they are rebuilt from ONNX with an arbitrary std, in which case they fall on their own and the learner learns to wait (cross-body xg1: 2.4 x more wins in training than losses, the reverse in eval). Use `--frozen-deterministic` then.

lessons.heading: Training lessons (G1, Kim, Trump; 2026-10-07 to 2026-10-20) › 3. Opponents and curricula
lessons.text: **Warm starts from an exported brain need a critic warm-up** (`--critic-warmup 10-20`): a random value function pushes a good actor away from what it does well.

lessons.heading: Training lessons (G1, Kim, Trump; 2026-10-07 to 2026-10-20) › 3. Opponents and curricula
lessons.text: **Start the pool easy and keep the easy opponents in it.** allround1 started from the brain that beats a standing opponent and kept that skill while learning to duel; leagues of chargers alone lost it.

lessons.heading: Training lessons (G1, Kim, Trump; 2026-10-07 to 2026-10-20) › 3. Opponents and curricula
lessons.text: **The league is not transitive**: beating the current champion is not beating everything before it (allround4 beat allround1 74 / 16 but did worse against gens 3-7). Judge a candidate on several opponents (`queue_options.sh suite()`).

lessons.heading: Training lessons (G1, Kim, Trump; 2026-10-07 to 2026-10-20) › 3. Opponents and curricula
lessons.text: **Clock-driven curricula can fade help before it is used** (getup2). `koth/curriculum.py` advances on the win share and steps back below a floor. With the opponent ladder the cross-body runs held their level for the first time (Trump vs the G1 league: 31 % wins / 49 % losses against fight1's 33 / 59; Kim 31 / 68 against 33 / 63), where three clock-driven recipes ended below their start. Kim needed a step back (stage 1 -> 0 at iteration 210) before she could advance. 400 iterations reached stage 2 of 4 for both: the ladder stops the drift, it does not yet add strength.

lessons.heading: Training lessons (G1, Kim, Trump; 2026-10-07 to 2026-10-20) › 4. Actions
lessons.text: **The champion's actions sit on the +-1 clamp 29 % of the time while torque is rarely the limit** (1.9 % of ticks): the ankles want ~2 rad of roll target against a 0.26 rad range. The humans' brains clamp ~2 %. Audit any new brain with `drive_audit.py --ckpt`.

lessons.heading: Training lessons (G1, Kim, Trump; 2026-10-07 to 2026-10-20) › 4. Actions
lessons.text: **Changing the action path of a trained brain is expensive.** 400-iteration fine-tunes of careful1: per-joint scale from its own raw outputs (scale1) kept level with the control (vs duel_u1 50 / 45) but lost to careful1 (35 / 63); tanh + torque window (mask1) lost 85 % to careful1. These options belong at the start of a new body's ladder, not in a champion's fine-tune; the sidecar mechanism (`<name>_action.json`) makes that safe in Unity.

lessons.heading: Training lessons (G1, Kim, Trump; 2026-10-07 to 2026-10-20) › 4. Actions
lessons.text: **One goal law, one set of commands.** Moving the goal point at run time (Tactician) lost to plain Press in every variant; training on random tactics (r4tactic) made the brain worse at Press (loses 85 % to careful1) within 400 iterations. A tactical layer needs its own training budget and its own gate.

lessons.heading: Training lessons (G1, Kim, Trump; 2026-10-07 to 2026-10-20) › 5. Observations and the Unity mirror
lessons.text: **Write only what the plugin can mirror** (no keyframes, contact pairs, `ls_iterations` written from C#), use primitive colliders, a convex mesh dome rather than an hfield (Warp makes one contact per hfield pair), and expect importer traps: ASCII-STL headers, default-class array tails (knee kv read as 0), `mass="0"` ignored on geoms, `OnSyncState` zeroing ctrl.

lessons.heading: Training lessons (G1, Kim, Trump; 2026-10-07 to 2026-10-20) › 5. Observations and the Unity mirror
lessons.text: **Unity's inputs match training for a body that meets its own kind** (two G1: mean drift <= 0.27 sd, KS <= 0.13). A human meeting other bodies is out of distribution**: Kim in the six-way game, 20 of 112 inputs over the bars (opponent distance and command KS 0.43, waist pitch 0.83 sd forward); Trump 8 of 112. Brains trained against their own body only: a game of mixed bodies needs cross-body training (section 3).

lessons.heading: Training lessons (G1, Kim, Trump; 2026-10-07 to 2026-10-20) › 5. Observations and the Unity mirror
lessons.text: **Spawns, noise and the out rule must match** between eval and Unity, or the statistics drift (FFA: more bell ties in Unity from spawn spacing and missing observation noise).

lessons.heading: Training lessons (G1, Kim, Trump; 2026-10-07 to 2026-10-20) › 6. Judging a run
lessons.text: One variable per run, against the same pool as the run it modifies (`queue_options.sh`: every G1 option repeated duel_u1's recipe, so duel_u1 was the control).

lessons.heading: Training lessons (G1, Kim, Trump; 2026-10-07 to 2026-10-20) › 6. Judging a run
lessons.text: Read the breakdown, not the headline: the "7.3 % self-ejection" was every loss (falls, tripping, the leg-contact rule); real self-ejection was 0.2 %.

lessons.heading: Training lessons (G1, Kim, Trump; 2026-10-07 to 2026-10-20) › 6. Judging a run

lessons.heading: Training lessons (G1, Kim, Trump; 2026-10-07 to 2026-10-20) › 6. Judging a run

lessons.heading: RL Optimization Log — September 2026 › 2026-09-27 · r1_v1 — FAILED (standing collapse) · r1_v2 prepared
lessons.text: **Root causes:** 1. *Warm-start normalizer:* the Rung 0 obs normalizer had var = 0 on command and gait-phase dims (constant in Rung 0) and count ≈ 1e8. lessons.heading: Architecture — PoPunkouterSoftware › Graphics and audio › Four bugs here that all failed silently — check for them before adding shader code
lessons.text: **An opaque `<body>` background hid every backdrop layer.** `#app-gpu-backdrop` and the `body::before` grid are both `position: fixed` with **negative** z-index, and negative-z descendants paint *before* an ancestor's in-flow block background. So `body` painting a colour covered both. The page colour now lives on `html`, and `html body` carries `background: transparent !important` — the `!important` is needed to beat something in the Radzen theme sheets. Proven by forcing the composite shader to solid opaque red and watching the page still render navy.

lessons.heading: Architecture — PoPunkouterSoftware › Graphics and audio › Four bugs here that all failed silently — check for them before adding shader code
lessons.text: **`smoothstep(hi, lo, x)` is undefined** in both GLSL and WGSL when `edge0 > edge1`. It compiles, the layer reports itself healthy, and the driver may return zero everywhere. Always write `1.0 - smoothstep(lo, hi, x)`.

lessons.heading: Architecture — PoPunkouterSoftware › Graphics and audio › Four bugs here that all failed silently — check for them before adding shader code
lessons.text: **`curl()` returns a true derivative** (the finite difference is divided by `2*epsilon`), so its magnitude is ~7, not ~1. Multiplying it by 0.085 displaced every sample point outside its own gaussian falloff and the whole field evaluated to zero — again with no error and no artefact. Check the *magnitude* of a noise term against the coordinate range it is perturbing.

lessons.heading: Architecture — PoPunkouterSoftware › Graphics and audio › Four bugs here that all failed silently — check for them before adding shader code
lessons.text: **The canvas is non-premultiplied** (`premultipliedAlpha: false`), so anything added to `col.rgb` in the composite is multiplied by the field's near-zero alpha on screen — an effect lands at roughly its intensity squared. The shockwave, sweep and burst glow were all invisible this way while the layer reported `webgl2`. Emissive terms go into `emit` and are folded in premultiplied at the end of `COMPOSITE_FS`. The same trap hid the particles themselves (their blend squared alpha), which is why the particle pass uses `blendFuncSeparate(SRC_ALPHA, ONE, ONE, ONE)`.

lessons.heading: Architecture — PoPunkouterSoftware › Things that will bite you
lessons.text: **One application stylesheet.** `wwwroot/css/modern-ui.css` is the whole thing (plus `boot.css` for the pre-Blazor splash). It was a four-line aggregator over `modern-ui.base/.components/.responsive`; CSS `@import` is serial, so the split cost three extra round trips on the critical path and bought nothing a section comment does not. lessons.heading: Architecture — PoPunkouterSoftware › Things that will bite you
lessons.text: **Scoped CSS does not cross component boundaries.** Blazor stamps the scope attribute only on the owning component's own elements, so moving markup from a page into a child component silently kills every scoped rule that styled it. `AzureDashboard.razor.css` is written as `.azure-ops-page ::deep …` for exactly that reason — keep **every** rule in that form, media-query overrides included. `::deep` also moves the scope attribute leftward, so mixing forms breaks specificity: `.azure-ops-page ::deep .x` compiles to `.azure-ops-page[b-id] .x` (0,3,0) while a bare `.x` compiles to `.x[b-id]` (0,2,0). Media queries add no specificity, so a bare override loses to its own base rule** and the layout

lessons.heading: Architecture — PoPunkouterSoftware › Things that will bite you
lessons.text: **A global rule that must beat a page-root scoped rule needs (0,2,1), not (0,2,0).** A page root such as `.azure-ops-page` carries a scoped rule compiling to `.azure-ops-page[b-hash]` — (0,2,0) — and `App.razor` loads `PoPunkouterSoftware.Client.styles.css` **after** `modern-ui.css`, so a global selector that merely ties loses the tie on document order. Prefix it with `html`. The removed phone pager learned this the hard way: its `display: block` lost to the scoped `display: grid`, the panes became grid rows a sixth of a screen tall painting over one another, and every E2E assertion that measured CONTENT still passed. Measure the rendered box.

lessons.heading: Architecture — PoPunkouterSoftware › Things that will bite you
lessons.text: **The Integration fixture must hand back a developer's local report.** `TestWebApp` sets `App_Data/azure-full-report.json` aside, seeds its own, and restores on dispose. Its `Dispose(true)` runs TWICE (`WebApplicationFactory` reaches it from `DisposeAsync` and `Dispose`), and until 2026-11-03 the second pass deleted the real report the first had just put back — every test run wiped the local cache. It clears its fields before touching a file, and it never moves aside a seed it finds in place.

lessons.heading: Architecture — PoPunkouterSoftware › Things that will bite you

lessons.heading: 1. Coding standard › 3. Reward Engineering & Motion Shaping › 3.3 The two shaping traps that have cost the most here
lessons.text: **A shaping term that saturates outside the range the policy occupies is not weak, it is ABSENT — and looks identical to weak from outside.** `WALK_TALL_Y` / `WALK_CROUCH_Y` were copied from the sumo school as 0.95/0.65 while the walking gait lives at 0.46–0.80, so the term was clamped to zero across nearly its entire operating range: the reward could not tell 0.60 from 0.55. Two full retrains were spent tuning the *strength* of something that was not connected. **Always check a new term's ramp against a measured distribution of the quantity it reads.** The same failure killed the first strike-impulse curve, which peaked at 11.9 m/s against measured strike speeds of 3.9–5.3 m/s.

lessons.heading: 1. Coding standard › 3. Reward Engineering & Motion Shaping › 3.3 The two shaping traps that have cost the most here
lessons.text: **You cannot out-shape a terminal.** In `Mode.Walk` a fall is `SetReward(-1)` plus the forgone `+3` graduation, about **−4**; the whole tall-vs-crawl per-step shaping advantage was **0.0063**. Break-even is 0.16% extra fall probability per step. If a shaped behaviour is more fall-prone than that, the degenerate behaviour is *correct play* and no reasonable coefficient changes it. Corollary, learned from the `gait01` run: **attacking the terminal instead does not work either.** Cheap falls do not buy exploration, because **a body already on the ground cannot fall** — once the policy found the floor, the fall terminal simply stopped firing and there was no gradient left pointing up.

lessons.heading: 1. Coding standard › 1.2 House rules › Policy Architecture & Retraining
lessons.text: **Hierarchy:** A few small policies, one per motor skill family (locomotion, balance/get-up, task skills). Cover variants with command inputs (velocity, gait, target, style), not new policies. Layered rule-based directors (game flow → body → skill) switch policies on physical state (contacts, centre of mass, falls) through one transition table, mirrored in every runtime. Policies never pick each other.

lessons.heading: 1. Coding standard › 1.2 House rules › Policy Architecture & Retraining
lessons.text: **Hand-overs:** All policies of a body share the observation layout, joint order, action map, timing and motion-style reward. Preload every policy. Pass on the last action; never snap poses or blend outputs. Train each policy on the states it inherits (get-up from real falls).

lessons.heading: 1. Coding standard › 1.2 House rules › Policy Architecture & Retraining

lessons.heading: 1. Coding standard › UU_AGENT rules › 2. Physics & Transform Conventions
lessons.text: **Coordinate & Unit Space:** UE5 uses Z-Up, Left-Handed coordinates in centimeters. MuJoCo / URLab uses Z-Up (or Y-Up depending on model XML), Right-Handed coordinates in meters. Apply an explicit 100× unit scale factor and axis transformation in the bridge layer.

lessons.heading: 1. Coding standard › UU_AGENT rules › 2. Physics & Transform Conventions
lessons.text: **Deterministic Allocation:** Pre-allocate all character skeletal meshes, ground collision surfaces, and props from simulation definitions at startup. Dynamic runtime spawning or actor destruction is forbidden.

lessons.heading: 1. Coding standard › UU_AGENT rules › 2. Physics & Transform Conventions

lessons.text: **Hierarchy:** Lean policies divided by motor skill family (Level 0 balance, locomotion, task skills). Variances are handled via command vectors (target velocity, gait style), not separate networks.

lessons.heading: 1. Coding standard › UU_AGENT rules › 3. Policy Architecture & Hand-Overs
lessons.text: **Directors:** Layered rule-based state machines (game flow → body state → skill selector) switch policies based on physical sensors (contact flags, center of mass, foot slip). Policies never switch or invoke each other directly.

lessons.heading: 1. Coding standard › UU_AGENT rules › 3. Policy Architecture & Hand-Overs
lessons.text: **Hand-Overs:** All policies for a given character share the observation space, joint ordering, action layout, step rate ($dt$), and style rewards. Preload all policies at level initialization. Carry over the last action vector; never snap poses or blend bone transforms. Train recovery/get-up skills starting from real simulated falls.

lessons.heading: 1. Coding standard › UU_AGENT rules › 3. Policy Architecture & Hand-Overs
lessons.text: **Interface Stability:** Append new observation features only at the end with zero-initialized weights; never reorder or delete inputs. Breakages require policy distillation.

lessons.heading: 1. Coding standard › UU_AGENT rules › 3. Policy Architecture & Hand-Overs

lessons.heading: 1. Coding standard › UU_AGENT rules › 4. Training, Gates & Optimization

lessons.heading: AGENTS.md — PoBox › 2. PoBox house rules and notes › 2.3 Physics & Quality Checks

lessons.heading: AGENTS.md — PoBox › 2. PoBox house rules and notes › 2.3 Physics & Quality Checks
lessons.text: **Collision:** Simple primitive shapes (capsules, boxes, spheres) fitted inside the skinned mesh; never the visual mesh or the bones. All parts collide with each other and the world except parent–child pairs and pairs that overlap in the default stance (joint limits handle those). Clear mesh separation: before training, verify no pair touches in the T-pose, the default stance and a normal arm and leg swing. Here: `Training/tools/check_self_collision.py`.*

lessons.heading: AGENTS.md — PoBox › 2. PoBox house rules and notes › 2.3 Physics & Quality Checks
lessons.text: **Action smoothing:** Promote human-like, fluid joint motion without jitter: torque/action-rate penalties, low-pass filtering of actions, or jerk minimisation in the reward. Here: every env charges the squared action change (`r["rate"]` in `envs/footwork.py`, `getup.py`, `boxing.py`); `train_box.py --action-rate-w` adds more. Low-pass action smoothing (`--action-filter`, `action_filter` / `drive_filter`) and observation delay (`--obs-delay-max`, `obs_delay_steps`) live in `envs/boxing.py`, `MjBoxer.Drive`, and `tools/set_brain_rules.py`.*

lessons.text: **Resource limits:** Save and commit before long training runs. Close Unity for runs over 30 minutes or when free RAM is below 4 GB. Never delete a run written in the last 24 hours or one a queue may resume. Here: one 4096-environment run at a time; follow the queue/checkpoint state before pruning anything.*

lessons.heading: 1. Coding standard › 1.3 House rules › 1.3.3 Physics, Collisions & Verification Gates
lessons.text: **Collision rules:** Primitive colliders only (capsules, spheres, boxes); never raw bones or visual meshes. Enable self-collision on every non-adjacent pair (all but direct parent-child). Ensure zero mesh penetration across rest pose, T-pose and joint limits (swing arcs). Here: `Training/scripts/collision_audit.py` → `SCREENSHOTS/collision-<YYMMDD>/report.html`.*

lessons.heading: 1. Coding standard › 1.3 House rules › 1.3.3 Physics, Collisions & Verification Gates
lessons.text: **Physical fidelity:** Use Earth gravity (−9.81 m/s²), anatomical mass, realistic joint, torque and speed limits; validate skinned meshes and keep rig hierarchies aligned with simulator joints.

lessons.heading: 1. Coding standard › 1.3 House rules › 1.3.3 Physics, Collisions & Verification Gates
lessons.text: **Action smoothing:** Promote human-like, fluid joint motion without jitter: torque/action-rate penalties, low-pass filtering of actions, or jerk minimisation in the reward. Here: the `action_rate` reward term (`koth/env.py`, -0.03 in the hill recipe) and the action low-pass `smooth` (`koth/action_map.py` = `ActionMap.cs`, carried in the brain's `_action.json`, `train.py --action-smooth`). Too much smoothing stalls mirror duels (log 2026-10-29, `scripts/sweep_smooth.py`): judge it by decided share, not only by jitter.*

lessons.heading: 1. Coding standard › 1.3 House rules › 1.3.3 Physics, Collisions & Verification Gates
lessons.text: **Model fidelity:** Keep rig hierarchies aligned with simulator joints. Here: MuJoCo is the only simulator; regenerate imported Unity models from the Python MJCF source and pass `ModelDumpCheck`.*

lessons.heading: 1. Coding standard › 1.3 House rules › 1.3.3 Physics, Collisions & Verification Gates
lessons.text: **Behaviour decomposition:** Split behaviours into a few small, separately trained ONNX policies (one per skill family: locomotion/fight, get-up, later kick or carry), never one giant do-everything network; steer each with command inputs (velocity, target, style) rather than adding a policy per variant. Every policy for a body shares the same observation layout, joint order and action map, so any of them can take over mid-motion. A rule-based director (state machine) above them picks the active policy from simulator state; policies never pick each other. Load and warm every policy at scene start and switch by changing which worker runs, never by loading a model mid-match. Keep the hand-over

lessons.heading: 1. Coding standard › 1.3 House rules › 1.3.3 Physics, Collisions & Verification Gates
lessons.text: **Build so changes do not force retraining from scratch:** Treat each policy's interface (observation order, joint order, action map) as a frozen contract: only append new inputs at the end, never reorder or remove them; if the contract must break, distil the old policy into the new layout instead of starting RL from zero. Put presentation, HUD, match flow and director rules outside the policies, so changing them needs only a re-gate, not training. Expose tunable game values (arena size, sea, friction, push strength) to training as randomized ranges, so a change inside the range needs no retraining and one outside it needs a fine-tune. When a policy must change, fine-tune it from the shipped

lessons.text: **Graduation gate:** Export an ONNX policy only when its target score holds for 100 consecutive episodes with zero NaN gradients. Here: a checkpoint is trusted only after its Unity gate too (trajectory parity or statistical parity, section 1.4).*

lessons.text: **Training telemetry:** Run TensorBoard with each training run, log metrics and progress, and estimate the run duration at startup.

lessons.heading: 1. Coding standard › 1.3 House rules › 1.3.4 Policy Architecture & Retraining
lessons.text: **Skill hierarchy:** Prefer a small policy per motor-skill family (locomotion, balance/get-up, task skills), with command inputs for variants rather than a new policy for every variant. A layered, rule-based director should switch skills from physical state through one transition table mirrored in every runtime; policies must not select other policies. Here: the current shipped runtime has per-body fighter and get-up brains. Preserve its Python/Unity parity; any move to shared skill policies or a transition table must update both sides and their gates together.*

lessons.heading: 1. Coding standard › 1.3 House rules › 1.3.4 Policy Architecture & Retraining
lessons.text: **Policy hand-overs:** Policies for a body must share observation layout, joint order, action map, timing and motion-style reward. Preload policies, pass the last action between them, avoid pose snaps or output blending, and train each policy on the states it inherits (including real falls for get-up).

lessons.heading: 1. Coding standard › 1.3 House rules › 1.3.4 Policy Architecture & Retraining
lessons.text: **Frozen interfaces:** Append observation inputs only at the end and zero-initialize their weights. Never reorder or remove existing inputs; if an interface break is unavoidable, distil the prior policy into the new layout.

lessons.heading: 1. Coding standard › 1.3 House rules › 1.3.4 Policy Architecture & Retraining
lessons.text: **Character independence:** Every new character gets its own training run and policies; do not reuse another character's brain, even for similar bodies. Train from scratch through every ladder level and gate against the existing roster. Personality comes from character traits and learned style-reward weights, not scripted director behavior. Once a character is trained, avoid fully retraining existing characters.

lessons.heading: 1. Coding standard › 1.3 House rules › 1.3.4 Policy Architecture & Retraining
lessons.text: **Checkpoint provenance and regression:** Tag every checkpoint with its observation/action interface and physics versions. After a change, rerun and record every affected policy's regression scenarios for both task performance and realism.

lessons.text: **One brain per character:** Every new character gets its own training run and its own policies. No character reuses another's brain, even when the bodies are similar. Personality comes from the character card's traits and its own style reward weights, learned in training. Directors don't script it. Each character trains from scratch, passes every ladder level and the gate, and trains against the existing roster. Once a character is trained, try to avoid retraining it fully.

lessons.text: **Show the physics viewer when training in MuJoCo or Isaac Lab.** Those trainers must run with their UI up so the creature's movement can be watched **during and after** training. A headless physics run hides precisely the failure this project has hit repeatedly — mean reward climbing while the body cannot actually move (the p17–p21 arc below; nine phases of hypotheses rested on a policy that could not cross the pitch). Unity ML-Agents runs stay headless for wall-clock reasons; the observability substitutes there are TensorBoard and `Agent_PlayMode_MovementProbe`, and both are mandatory, not optional.

lessons.heading: CLAUDE.md › Hard rules (UNITY_AGENT / UNITY_RULES)
lessons.text: **Creatures move realistically.** Physical bodies use **Earth gravity**, joint articulation limited to real anatomical ranges, and **mass scaled to body size**. Drive force scales with mass so every physique shares one top speed and a heavier body simply carries more momentum — never a uniform force that makes big creatures sluggish and small ones twitchy. PoSoccer's top-down plane is the one standing exemption (zero in-plane gravity, recorded in `docs/rules-exemptions.md`); gravity still enters physically through the `mu * m * g` traction budget.

lessons.heading: 1. Coding standard › 2. C# Simulation & Biomechanical Constraints › 2.2 Muscle & torque limits
lessons.text: **No infinite-force motors.** `maximumForce = Mathf.Infinity` (3D) or an unbounded `maxMotorTorque` (2D) produces superhuman leverage and violent twitching. Every motor carries a finite budget.

lessons.heading: 1. Coding standard › 2. C# Simulation & Biomechanical Constraints › 2.2 Muscle & torque limits
lessons.text: **Force-velocity (Hill).** Concentric torque falls off with contraction speed; eccentric bracing keeps its 1.5x gain. Implemented in `ApplyMotor`.

lessons.heading: 1. Coding standard › 2. C# Simulation & Biomechanical Constraints › 2.2 Muscle & torque limits
lessons.text: **Fatigue.** Each joint carries a 0..1 fatigue state integrated at 50 Hz (`IntegrateFatigue`, the two-state reduction of Xia's three-compartment muscle model: `FATIGUE_RATE` 0.06/s, `RECOVERY_RATE` 0.10/s, `FATIGUE_DEPTH` 0.35). Load is read from `joint.GetMotorTorque(dt)`, never from the action vector** — isometric bracing is a near-zero action holding a near-maximum torque, and any action-derived measure would score the most expensive thing in a bout as resting.

lessons.heading: 1. Coding standard › 2. C# Simulation & Biomechanical Constraints › 2.2 Muscle & torque limits
lessons.text: **Activation lag.** Torque *and* the velocity target are both smoothed. Smoothing only the torque while writing `motorSpeed` straight from the action leaves a perfectly crisp velocity command, and the jitter comes back through the other door.

lessons.heading: 1. Coding standard › 2. C# Simulation & Biomechanical Constraints › 2.2 Muscle & torque limits
lessons.text: **Passive resistance.** Real joints are not frictionless linkages: a restoring torque at 6% of each joint's motor budget per 90°, plus 10% per 400°/s of damping, applied every `FixedUpdate`. (`HingeJoint2D` has no spring — that is 3D-only — hence the explicit torque.) Bodies damp at 0.25 linear / 0.8 angular.

lessons.heading: 1. Coding standard › 2. C# Simulation & Biomechanical Constraints › 2.3 Anatomical limits & action normalization
lessons.text: Actions are **13 continuous values in [−1, 1]** (`Agent_Biped.ActionCount`), mapped into each joint's own biological range. Never let an action index outrun the joint table: `ApplyMotor` indexes `0..ActionCount-1`, so the 2 unpowered toe (MTP) hinges must stay last** in `JOINT_DEFS`.

lessons.heading: 1. Coding standard › 2. C# Simulation & Biomechanical Constraints › 2.3 Anatomical limits & action normalization
lessons.text: **Anchors derive from segment lengths.** Change a segment length and every anchor above it moves with it, or the chain comes apart. Verify by measuring anchor separation across all joints — it must read 0.0000 m.

lessons.heading: 1. Coding standard › 2. C# Simulation & Biomechanical Constraints › 2.3 Anatomical limits & action normalization
lessons.text: **Verify joint ranges parent-local, never in world space.** With gravity off the whole body counter-rotates to conserve angular momentum, so a world-space test reads the body's drift, not the joint. Use `parent.transform.InverseTransformPoint(child.position)` at rest and at full flexion and compare the delta — that is rotation-invariant.

lessons.heading: 1. Coding standard › 2. C# Simulation & Biomechanical Constraints › 2.3 Anatomical limits & action normalization
lessons.text: **The sign convention is measured, not guessed.** `HingeJoint2D.jointAngle` here is the negative** of the child's geometric rotation relative to its parent. Ranges written as if geometric bend the limb *backwards* — this shipped a bird leg for the whole early life of the project. Current: hip (−120…30°), knee (0…150°), elbow (−150…0°), ankle (−20…50°), spine (−12…30° each), shoulder (−175…60°), toe (−60…30°). `JOINT_DEFS` is the authority; these four were symmetric until 2026-09-05. `Agent_Biped.KneeBendFactor()` reads the knee as positive and must move with these.

lessons.heading: 1. Coding standard › 2. C# Simulation & Biomechanical Constraints › 2.5 Ground interaction & anti-skating
lessons.text: **Real friction materials.** `PhysicsMaterial2D` — feet 0.9, body 0.4, bounciness 0 on both (`Agent_BipedBody`, ~L554). Surface friction is domain-randomized per round by `Systems_SumoMatchManager`; the rim `tawara` band is deliberately low-friction.

lessons.heading: 1. Coding standard › 2. C# Simulation & Biomechanical Constraints › 2.5 Ground interaction & anti-skating
lessons.text: **Stance tracking is height AND speed, and both are arena-relative.** `Reward_StepCadence` counts a foot planted below `PLANTED_HEIGHT` 0.12 m **relative to the arena ground**, moving slower than `PLANTED_SPEED` 0.5 m/s, and pays only on an alternation of the single planted foot, with `MIN_STEP_INTERVAL` 0.25 s between paid steps. Measured against absolute world Y this term was meaningless for the walk lane at y = −60 — every foot was trivially "below" threshold, plantedness collapsed to the velocity gate alone, and the airborne apex of a swing scored as a step, while the same line behaved correctly in the sumo lane at y = 0. **Any new contact or height test must be arena-relative.**

lessons.heading: 1. Coding standard › 2. C# Simulation & Biomechanical Constraints › 2.5 Ground interaction & anti-skating
lessons.text: Per-foot contact and normal force come from the feet's own contact lists into a preallocated `ContactPoint2D[]` (`_contactBuf`, size 8) — **no allocation in `FixedUpdate`**. Non-foot parts report ground contact through `Sensor_BodyPartContact`.

lessons.heading: 1. Coding standard › 2. C# Simulation & Biomechanical Constraints › 2.5 Ground interaction & anti-skating
lessons.text: **Penalize relative linear velocity at a contacting foot**, not merely "foot is moving". A planted foot sliding under load is the skate; a swing foot moving fast is correct gait.

lessons.heading: 1. Coding standard › 2. C# Simulation & Biomechanical Constraints › 2.6 Upright posture & centre of mass
lessons.text: **Never freeze `Rigidbody` rotation axes** to keep a body upright, and never add an invisible stabilising torque the policy cannot observe. Balance is an outcome, not a constraint. Monitor CoM trajectory, pelvis alignment and ground reaction force, and reward* them.

lessons.heading: 1. Coding standard › 2. C# Simulation & Biomechanical Constraints › 2.6 Upright posture & centre of mass
lessons.text: Uprightness is shaped; falling is terminal (Walk school only). Trunk height is read arena-relative; standing pose is ~1.06 m for the 1.76 m / 69.6 kg baseline body.

lessons.heading: 1. Coding standard › 2. C# Simulation & Biomechanical Constraints › 2.6 Upright posture & centre of mass

lessons.heading: 1. Coding standard › 4. Build & Training Commands › 4.3 Train
lessons.text: `--resume` — parameter-only tweaks. A `--resume` into a config whose `max_steps` already equals the checkpoint's step count **exits immediately having trained nothing and looks exactly like a successful short run**.

lessons.heading: 1. Coding standard › 4. Build & Training Commands › 4.3 Train
lessons.text: `--force` — physics, observation or action changes (or use a new run-id). Kill TensorBoard first.** It holds Windows handles on the run dirs, and a `--force` fired while it is live leaves the old contents *in place*, silently — after which the surviving checkpoints outrank the new run numerically and a deploy ships a brain from the run you thought you deleted.

lessons.heading: 1. Coding standard › 4. Build & Training Commands › 4.3 Train
lessons.text: `--base-port` — **always explicit.** The trainer takes `--num-envs` consecutive ports from there; two runs on the default 5005 collide and the second hangs on a handshake the first already answered. Space concurrent runs by at least `--num-envs` (5005, 5015, 5025 …).

lessons.heading: 1. Coding standard › 4. Build & Training Commands › 4.3 Train
lessons.text: `--num-envs` — a CPU budget, 4–8 on a 12-core box, leaving cores for torch threads. Not a pure throughput dial**: changing it changes how experience is batched and therefore changes the resulting model. Record the value in the config header.

lessons.heading: 1. Coding standard › 4. Build & Training Commands › 4.5 Judging a run
lessons.text: **Self-play fight runs are judged on ELO, not mean reward.** The two move in opposite directions when a policy learns to farm shaping instead of winning bouts: one re-tune climbed to reward ~36 while its ELO fell 1198 → 1140. Mean reward is measured against a moving opponent pool and is not comparable across runs.

lessons.heading: 1. Coding standard › 4. Build & Training Commands › 4.5 Judging a run
lessons.text: Accept on the **shape** of the ELO curve: a monotonic slide is regression; oscillation within a point or two of the start is noise (flat ELO against a pool that is itself retraining means the policy kept pace).

lessons.heading: 1. Coding standard › 4. Build & Training Commands › 4.5 Judging a run
lessons.text: **Watch for the terminal-firing-every-episode signature:** mean reward pinned just under a graduation bonus with near-zero variance (one fighter sat at 2.999 ± 0.015). That is not a policy converging, it is one terminal firing every episode. Assert `StepCount` climbs, not just `CompletedEpisodes`.

lessons.heading: 1. Coding standard › 4. Build & Training Commands › 4.5 Judging a run
lessons.text: Behavioural claims are reported as a `MatchTestHarness.Run(n)` tally or a Game-view screenshot, never as an impression. The EditMode suite covers only two pure functions, and **a green run is not evidence that a body, reward or brain change works**.

lessons.heading: 1. Coding standard › 5. File Integrity & Exclusions › Expose tuning through serialized fields and ScriptableObjects
lessons.text: **When adding a shaping coefficient, default it to the constant the code used before**, so an untuned character keeps training exactly what it always did. That is what makes it safe to add these mid-project.

lessons.heading: 1. Coding standard › 5. File Integrity & Exclusions › Expose tuning through serialized fields and ScriptableObjects
lessons.text: **Tune the asset, not the serialized scene value.** Scene components copy from `GameTuning` in `Start`, so the `.unity` files hold stale copies that are overwritten at runtime and will mislead anyone grepping them.

lessons.heading: PoSumo — Design Spec › Rules
lessons.text: **Ring-out only:** you lose when your torso crosses the ring edge (x = ±7 m).

lessons.heading: PoSumo — Design Spec › Rules
lessons.text: Falling down is not a loss — the round continues until ring-out or the 30 s timeout (timeout = draw).
